rubric.label: Course understanding
rubric.description: Applies Inclusive business accurately to this case; the exact term need not be named if the idea is clearly used.

rubric.label: Decision
rubric.description: Treat it as inclusive because serving an underserved need is the primary purpose and the model always sustains itself.

rubric.label: Case evidence and reasoning
rubric.description: Uses a specific fact from the case and explains why it supports the decision: Financial sustainability keeps the social solution available; the underserved need determines what the model is built to do.

key.explanation: An inclusive business must always do both: meet a specific need of underserved people, and remain financially sustainable.

rubric.label: Course understanding
rubric.description: Applies No-frills healthcare access accurately to this case; the exact term need not be named if the idea is clearly used.

rubric.label: Decision
rubric.description: Locate a quality-controlled facility nearer the population, cutting only costs that leave essential care intact.

rubric.label: Case evidence and reasoning
rubric.description: Uses a specific fact from the case and explains why it supports the decision: Where care is located changes who can use it; cost discipline matters only if essential quality and access remain intact.

key.explanation: Vaatsalya placed low-cost hospitals in semi-urban areas to cut patients' travel burden, trimming only costs that left essential quality intact.

rubric.label: Governing ideas
rubric.description: Identifies locating focused secondary capacity near the underserved population, separating standardisable work from the scarce specialist to raise throughput, and the absence of a counterfactual in the impact claim.

rubric.label: Use of the numbers
rubric.description: Cites specific figures — 44% travelling over 90 km, ₹38,000 against ₹11,000 per delivery, 61% occupancy in tertiary units, 70% of surgeon time on non-surgical work, the nine-week list, or the 22 paramedical staff on reception.

rubric.label: How the ideas connect
rubric.description: Connects them: the access problem and the capacity problem are separate constraints with separate fixes, and neither is evidenced by the earnings claim as it stands.

rubric.label: The decision
rubric.description: Supports the semi-urban secondary network for the routine load, recommends redistributing non-surgical tasks to the existing paramedical staff, and declines to rest expansion on the current impact claim.

rubric.label: What would change it
rubric.description: Names what evidence would support the impact claim — a comparison group similar before treatment — or the conditions under which the cost discipline would start to threaten essential quality.

key.explanation: Where the next hospital should go

rubric.label: Course understanding
rubric.description: Applies Process specialisation in healthcare accurately to this case; the exact term need not be named if the idea is clearly used.

rubric.label: Decision
rubric.description: Separate standardisable tasks for trained support staff so the specialist concentrates on the constrained surgical step.

rubric.label: Case evidence and reasoning
rubric.description: Uses a specific fact from the case and explains why it supports the decision: Specialisation raises throughput when routine work is separated from the scarce expert task without lowering clinical quality.

key.explanation: Aravind standardised pre- and post-operative work for paramedics so surgeons focused on surgery, never at the cost of clinical quality.

rubric.label: Decision
rubric.description: Track pollution reduction, product economics and worker livelihoods, which count as shared value only when all three hold.

rubric.label: Case evidence and reasoning
rubric.description: Uses a specific fact from the case and explains why it supports the decision: Waste becomes shared value only when material recovery, customer demand, and worker welfare reinforce one another.

key.explanation: An inclusive waste enterprise creates shared value only when recovery, product demand and worker livelihoods all hold together.

rubric.label: Course understanding
rubric.description: Applies Impact investing accurately to this case; the exact term need not be named if the idea is clearly used.

rubric.label: Decision
rubric.description: Classify it as impact investing because intent, measurement and return are all designed together.

rubric.label: Case evidence and reasoning
rubric.description: Uses a specific fact from the case and explains why it supports the decision: Intent defines the desired change, measurement tests whether it occurred, and return keeps investment capital reusable.

key.explanation: Impact investing needs all three of intent, measurement and financial return present together; it is never a grant.

rubric.label: Course understanding
rubric.description: Applies Group-based microfinance accurately to this case; the exact term need not be named if the idea is clearly used.

rubric.label: Decision
rubric.description: Use formed groups, staged lending and local monitoring, which works only while repayment capacity stays real.

rubric.label: Case evidence and reasoning
rubric.description: Uses a specific fact from the case and explains why it supports the decision: Local information can reduce screening risk, but the structure works only when repayment capacity and group discipline remain real.

key.explanation: The classic Grameen model lent without collateral using group knowledge and peer accountability, which holds only while repayment capacity stays real.

rubric.label: Course understanding
rubric.description: Applies Responsible lending accurately to this case; the exact term need not be named if the idea is clearly used.

rubric.label: Decision
rubric.description: Pause lending, assess total obligations and cash flow, and never let volume incentives outrun borrower capacity.

rubric.label: Case evidence and reasoning
rubric.description: Uses a specific fact from the case and explains why it supports the decision: Access becomes harmful when debt service outruns income; scale must preserve the screening practices that made inclusion viable.

key.explanation: Responsible lending checks total debt and repayment capacity, and never lets loan volume outrun the screening that made inclusion viable.
